This role owns how local marketing gets activated for FWA HSI: partnering with the HSI acquisition team to identify opportunities and priorities, deciding where, why, and how to activate, designing the programs that do it, and enabling the field to run those programs with confidence.

The role works where network capacity and demand are out of balance. That includes High Supply and Low Demand markets, where available capacity isn’t converting into activations, and markets where churn and disconnects are eroding growth. This person turns market-level data into targeted local programs, runs them, measures them, and scales what works.

This is not a project coordinator role. This person builds the activation programs, owns their delivery, and is accountable for whether they drive new accounts and retention in market.

This is a remote role. Travel expectation is up to 30% nationally, covering market visits, National Marketing engagements, planning sessions, and team collaboration. The best activation programs are designed by people who spend time in the markets they are building.


Job Responsibilities

Activation Strategy & Program Design



Own the activation approach. Develop the framework for how FWA HSI local marketing gets activated: which markets, which audiences, which tactics, in what sequence, and what principles guide local decisions.Lead High Supply and Low Demand programs. Combine network capacity data with local marketing levers to build programs that convert available capacity into activation and define when a geography qualifies.Build complete program designs. Every program should have a clear objective, target audience, channel mix, offer and messaging direction, timeline, budget, and success metric, with rationale for each choice.Develop retention-oriented programs. Partner with the disconnect and churn effort to design local programs that reduce HSI churn, not just drive new orders.Close the gaps. Identify moments where the organization lacks a proven tactic or a defined approach for FWA HSI, and build the solution instead of flagging it for someone else.


Program Execution & Field Enablement

Run the programs. Own program management from design through launch and close-out: timelines, dependencies, vendors, budgets, and cross-functional deliverables.Enable the field. Give the field everything it needs to execute: program briefs, targeting lists, messaging guidance, creative assets, and clear success criteria.Sequence the rollout. Pilot first, then scale in phases, tied to the commercial calendar and to the team’s 2027 expansion into HSI.Make it stick. Partner with the Hyperlocal Playbook Manager so proven programs are captured in the playbook as operating standards.


Measurement & Test-and-Learn

Design the tests. Build test-and-control structures for local programs so the team can separate real lift from noise.Target with data. Use propensity and segmentation analysis to choose and size markets and opportunity.Report what works. Produce clear readouts on incremental new accounts, churn impact, cost per acquisition, and program ROI, and recommend scale, adjust, or stop.Close the loop. Run a retrospective at the end of each program and each quarter: what the program produced, where execution diverged from the plan, and what changes next.


Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with National Marketing. Pull national campaigns, brand guardrails, and creative into field-ready formats, and push field learnings back up so what gets built centrally serves local needs.Partner with HSI Acquisition team to identify commercial opportunities and priorities for hyperlocal marketing campaignsPartner with Network and Capacity Planning. Get timely, usable capacity data so programs target the right markets at the right time.Partner with Analytics and Sales Operations. Align on data, measurement, and incentives so programs are measurable and the frontline is incented to action off of them.Coordinate with the Fiber team. Manage the places where FWA and fiber overlap, including footprint eligibility changes and creating an ecosystem accounting for customer moves from HSI to fiber.Steward the brand. Ensure local activity stays within T-Mobile brand guardrails while remaining locally effective.


Quarterly Planning & Field Intelligence

Contribute to the planning cycle. Translate commercial targets, capacity conditions, and national priorities into a 90-day activation program plan with market-by-market priorities.Synthesize the signal. Aggregate market observations, competitive activity, and program performance into insights that inform local decisions and national direction.Find the pattern. Identify which market conditions, audiences, and tactic combinations are producing results and what the team should do more of.Brief leadership. Produce a regular update for the Sr. Manager and Director on what’s working, what isn’t, and what the field needs.



Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree and 7 years of related work experience, or a combination of education and experience deemed equivalent7-10 years in marketing strategy, field marketing, growth marketing, or program management, with demonstrated ownership of programs from design through measurement.Strong analytical skills, including campaign measurement, segmentation, and test-and-control design.Experience managing complex, cross-functional programs with many stakeholders and no direct authority.Experience translating strategy into field-executable programs that people actually use.Strong written and verbal communicator who can brief the field, partner teams, and senior leaders.Comfortable operating without complete information and adjusting quickly when results come in.Experience in telecom, broadband, or a brand with a significant field or local marketing component preferredBackground managing the interface between a national marketing organization and a distributed field team preferredFamiliarity with hyperlocal marketing channels — OOH, community partnerships, ambassador programs, geo-targeted digital preferredExperience developing audience segmentation frameworks and channel-audience matching strategies preferredBackground in capability building — has developed training, toolkits, or frameworks adopted by a field team preferred At least 18 years of ageLegally authorized to work in the United States

      GDIT is seeking an experienced, scientifically fluent Senior Communications & Outreach Specialist to support a government contract with the NIH Office of Research Innovation, Validation, and Application (ORIVA). GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career.

About the Role

Reporting to the VP of Corporate and Product Marketing, you will define and drive a differentiated corporate story that increases LeanData's visibility, credibility, and category leadership in GTM orchestration. You will partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Customer Marketing, and executive leadership to ensure a consistent, compelling brand and message across every channel and audience — RevOps, Marketing Ops, Sales Development, and VP/CRO-level buyers.

This is a player-coach role. You will set strategy, produce and edit high-quality work yourself, and lead a small team plus agency and creative partners. If you are a strong storyteller, strategic content marketer and brand steward who can move fluidly in a fast-paced environment, keep reading.



Santa Clara, CA (Hybrid - M/W)  ·  Reports to the VP of Corporate and Product Marketing



What You'll Do

Corporate Narrative & Thought Leadership

Own and evolve LeanData's corporate narrative and messaging, ensuring a clear, differentiated story that ladders up from product and campaign messaging to the company vision.

Build and run an executive thought leadership program, ghostwriting and shaping bylines, keynotes, LinkedIn content, and points of view for the CMO, CEO, and other leaders.

Establish LeanData's voice on the category-defining conversations in GTM orchestration, RevOps, and AI.

Brand & Creative

Serve as steward of the LeanData brand — visual identity, voice, tone, and standards — ensuring consistency across web, product, sales, events, and social.

Direct creative and design execution (in-house and agency) for campaigns, corporate assets, and brand moments, including OpsStars.

Lead brand governance and rollout of updated positioning, guidelines, and templates across the organization.

Content Marketing & Editorial

Own content strategy and roadmap through the buyer journey, across formats and distribution channels

Manage development of long-form assets, blog, and video — mapped to business objectives, launches, and events.

Build G2 and other third-party category reports into the content calendar, turning each release into timely assets, campaigns, and AEO-ready proof points that reinforce LeanData’s category leadership.

Ensure content is high-quality, on-brand, SEO/AEO-optimized, and tied to pipeline and awareness goals.

Marketing Communications & PR

Lead PR strategy and the agency relationship to accelerate LeanData's market position and share of voice among prospects, partners, and press.

Own corporate communications, ensuring company announcements and internal communications drive alignment and excitement.

Develop and own the process for crisis and issues communications.

Influencer & Owned Channels

Build relationships with industry influencers and community voices to elevate the brand and drive awareness.

Own organic social and employee advocacy strategy across LeanData's corporate channels to grow and engage the audience.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Alignment

Lead, coach, and grow the corporate marketing team as a hands-on player-coach across content, brand, and communications.

Partner with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Customer Marketing, Sales, and executives to align the corporate story with GTM priorities.

Track and report on brand, share of voice, content, and communications performance, using insight to continuously optimize.

Experience & Required Skills

8+ years of marketing experience in B2B SaaS or technology, with at least 2–3 years leading and developing people.

Demonstrated ownership across corporate marketing disciplines — brand, content, and communications/PR — ideally with analyst or influencer relations exposure.

Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to translate complex topics into a clear, compelling narrative for GTM leaders (RevOps, Marketing Ops, Sales Ops, VP/CRO).

Proven brand stewardship — you can build and enforce voice, tone, and visual standards across a company.

Experience managing PR and creative agencies and delivering measurable share-of-voice and awareness outcomes.

Track record partnering cross-functionally with Product Marketing, Demand Gen, Sales, and executive leadership.

Comfort using AI tools to create, refine, and scale content and communications.

Strong project management and the ability to move fluidly between strategy and hands-on execution in a fast-paced environment.

Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, English, or a related field.

Nice to Have

Experience in the sales/marketing technology or RevOps space.

Experience building or scaling an executive thought leadership program.

Familiarity with the modern marketing stack (HubSpot, WordPress, Sprout Social, G2, Salesforce).

Experience marketing a company through a category-defining or repositioning moment.

Success Looks Like

Please Submit A Cover Letter





 About Us Lab Coat Marketing:
 We are a marketing firm built on the scientific method. Every experiment, every strategy, and every campaign is rooted in testing, truth-seeking, and results. Our mission: to be world-class in the two industries we serve.


 To get there, we only hire world-class candidates. The kind of people Steve Jobs meant when he said “A+ players like working with A+ players.” We are building a team of A-players, and our next hire — employee #9 — will play a pivotal role.





 About You:
 You’re not looking for a job. You’re looking for a team that unlocks your potential.


 You’re detail-oriented, fast without being sloppy, and ambitious enough to see yourself as a senior strategist within 3–5 years. You won’t be just ‘another marketer.’ You’ll join a hand-picked group where every seat matters. Your work will be visible, celebrated, and impactful.


 You don’t just “do tasks.” You:


 
 Notice what others miss. Accuracy matters, even when moving fast.
 Solve problems others can’t. You make it look effortless because you’re having fun.
 Deliver with speed and quality. You believe the secret is 99% perspiration, 1% inspiration.
 Uplift teammates. Your presence raises the bar for everyone around you.
 



 What You’ll Do (Starting Point)
 
 Marketing setups (ads, campaigns, tracking, integrations)
 Marketing & data analysis
 Some content writing
 Manage a small set of Google Ad accounts
 Perform QA checks across campaigns and deliverables
 Grow into client communication (after 6 months, once you’ve demonstrated mastery)
 



 Trajectory:
 We’re not hiring you for who you are today — we’re hiring you for who you can become. Your mission: become a world-class marketer within 3–5 years. We’ll give you the tools, the mentorship, and the environment. The rest is up to you.





 Bonus skills we would love to add to the team:
 
 Canva or other basic design software
 Google Sheets wizardry
 Experience with no-code tools or APIs
 You know who David Ogilvy or Claude Hopkins are — without needing to Google it
 



 Why This Role Is Different
 
 You’ll be the 9th member of a tight, ambitious, and fast growing team. You won’t be a cog — you’ll be a cornerstone.
 We treat marketing like science — testing, measuring, learning.
 We hire slowly, we hire right. If you’re reading this and feel that “this was written for me,” you’re probably who we’re looking for.
 



 What We Offer
 
 Starting Pay: $17.50–$24/hour (or up to $50K salary depending on experience)
 Health Benefits: 100% covered health/vision/dental after probation.
 Remote Work: Remote work with equipment provided.
 Flexible Hours: Flexible hours after 90 days.
 Company Culture: A culture of truth, loyalty, and experimentation.
 Mentorship: The chance to be mentored into a strategist, not stuck in “entry-level” forever.
 



 Our Core Values & Ethics
 Guiding Principles:
 At Lab Coat Marketing, our work is rooted in integrity, innovation, and service. We believe in:


 
 Getting Client Results: We measure success by the tangible impact we deliver.
 Loyalty to Clients & Each Other: Trust is non-negotiable—we advocate fiercely for our clients and support our team unconditionally.
 Being Truth Seekers: We ask hard questions, challenge assumptions, and prioritize honesty in every decision.
 



 What We Look For in You:
 
 Smart Problem-Solving: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and embrace the chance to explore unanswered questions
 Creative Experimentation: You bring curiosity and courage to test bold ideas (failure is just a step toward innovation).
 Hardworking Dedication: You’re driven by purpose, not just tasks—our clients’ success is your success.
 Team-Oriented: You’ve been on teams your whole life, where competing hard, celebrating wins, and lifting each other up taught you that true success comes from working together toward a common goal.

remotedirectorinternalcommunicationsupst.title: Remote Director, Internal Communications
remotedirectorinternalcommunicationsupst.description:
About Upstart


At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.


As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.


We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.


If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team: 


Upstart is looking for a Director of Internal Communications to evolve how employees understand the business we are building, how the company is performing and what our next chapter requires from them. Internal communications here is not a distribution function. It is a strategic capability that connects company decisions to our strategy, creates clarity during consequential moments and helps employees act with confidence.


 


You will join Upstart’s Communications, Culture & Development team, which helps employees understand where the company is going, feel connected to its purpose and build the capabilities to do their best work. You will evolve the strategy and operating rhythm for enterprise communications, serve as a senior partner to executives and functional leaders, and independently lead some of Upstart’s most consequential employee-facing work.


 


You will also own Upstart’s company knowledge strategy and core internal content portfolio, ensuring employees can find clear, current and trusted information across Guru and Glean. As our ways of working evolve, you will bring greater depth and thought leadership to our employee-facing GenAI communications and enablement strategy.


 


This is a role for a senior player-coach who sees beyond the immediate request, brings a strong point of view and stays close enough to the work to make the strategy real.


 


How you’ll make an impact



Evolve Upstart’s internal communications strategy and operating rhythm, including an enterprise employee calendar and governance practices that improve prioritization, timing and coordination.
Translate complex company priorities, performance and decisions into clear narratives that help employees understand where Upstart is headed, why it matters and what is expected of them.
Serve as a senior communications partner to the VP of Communications, Culture & Development and to executives and functional leaders on employee communications within the role’s portfolio.
Lead the strategy and end-to-end development of employee earnings communications, including the post-earnings all-hands, in partnership with Investor Relations, External Communications, Finance and senior leaders.
Build proactive communications strategies for priority company goals and enterprise changes, ensuring employees are brought along with clarity and appropriate context.
Own Upstart’s company knowledge strategy and core internal content portfolio. Establish the information architecture, editorial standards, governance and content lifecycle across Guru, Glean and emerging AI-enabled knowledge experiences.
Directly lead priority enterprise content while creating clear standards and accountability for specialized content owned by functions across Upstart.
Own the employee-facing GenAI communications and enablement strategy, helping employees understand how GenAI is changing the way we work and ensuring they are supported through that change.
Elevate flagship employee storytelling and connection through programs including Upstart Unlocked, Board and Lead-to-Lead conversations, ERG infrastructure, and employee recognition and anniversary experiences.
Partner closely with the Senior Manager of Internal Communications on TGIF, recurring employee communications, channel strategy, employer-brand storytelling and campaign execution.
Strengthen the function’s systems, measurement and decision rights so the team can operate with greater focus, consistency and impact.
Stay close to the work. Write, edit and deliver high-stakes communications; build the first version when something new is needed; and create repeatable approaches that allow the function to scale without sacrificing quality.
 

 


Minimum Qualifications 



10+ years of experience in internal communications, executive communications, change communications or a related field, including experience operating at a senior strategic level in a complex organization.
Exceptional writing and editing skills, paired with the judgment to make complicated business topics clear without making them simplistic.
Experience counseling senior executives and the confidence to challenge, advise and improve a leader’s communication while preserving their voice and intent.
Strong business and financial fluency, including experience translating company performance, strategy and consequential organizational decisions for employees.
Demonstrated experience building communications strategies, planning rhythms and operating systems, not only executing individual campaigns or managing channels.
The ability to lead complex cross-functional work, influence without direct authority and make thoughtful tradeoffs across timing, message design and employee burden.
Experience leading, coaching or developing experienced communications talent.
The ability and willingness to move between strategy and execution, including personally writing and delivering high-priority work.
Strong judgment, intellectual curiosity and comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where the right path may not yet be defined.

 


Preferred Qualifications



Experience with employee knowledge management, content governance, enterprise search or platforms such as Guru and Glean.
Experience developing communications or enablement strategies related to GenAI, digital transformation or significant changes in how employees work.
Experience in a public company, financial services, a regulated industry or another environment requiring close partnership with Investor Relations, Legal and Finance.
Experience supporting a distributed or digital-first workforce.

 


Position Location - This role is available in the following locations: Remote, Burlingame, CA, and Columbus, OH


Time Zone Requirements - This team operates on the East/West Coast time zones.


Travel Requirements - As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies, but in this role you can expect to travel 1-2 times per quarter.


 


At Upstart, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. The anticipated base salary for this position is expected to be within the below range. Your actual base pay will depend on your geographic location–with our “digital first” philosophy, Upstart uses compensation regions that vary depending on location. Individual pay is also determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.


In addition, Upstart provides employees with target bonuses, equity compensation, and generous benefits packages (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k).

$195,800 - $271,000 USD

What you'll love


At Upstart, our benefits for full-time employees are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here’s what you can expect:



Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly

For roles based in Canada, please note that we are not currently able to hire in Quebec.

strategicpartnershipsmanagerdigitalmarke.title: Strategic Partnerships Manager: Digital Marketing Agency/Influencer Partners
strategicpartnershipsmanagerdigitalmarke.description:
As Strategic Partnerships Manager: Analyst and Agency Partners, you own Intuit's commercial relationships with two distinct partner segments that sit at the edges of the mid-market ERP ecosystem: independent ERP analysts, and digital marketing agencies whose client base includes mid-market businesses evaluating ERP solutions.

ERP analysts in the mid-market are not the large research firms — they are independent voices: channel consultants, software selection advisors, and influential commentators who cover mid-market ERP platforms, shape buyer decisions, and maintain active networks of prospects and VARs. They generate a steady flow of referral introductions to buyers who trust their judgment. Building relationships with the right analysts and turning those relationships into a consistent pipeline of qualified warm introductions is the core of this motion.

Digital marketing agencies represent a different but equally valuable opportunity. Many agencies serve mid-market clients who need ERP solutions as part of broader digital transformation work — and those agencies need somewhere to route those leads. This role builds the program and relationships that make Intuit the natural destination for those introductions.

Both motions share the same KPI: qualified warm introductions attributable to a specific analyst or agency partner. You are not accountable for closed-won revenue — you are accountable for the quality and volume of the pipeline you generate through these relationships.

PRIMARY KPI: Qualified warm introductions attributable to a specific analyst or agency partner — defined as a mid-market prospect introduction where an IES, QuickBooks Advanced, or Intuit Services opportunity has been identified. Measured separately for analyst and agency segments.



 Responsibilities 

ERP analyst relationships

 Identify and map the independent ERP analyst community relevant to Intuit's mid-market segment: channel consultants, software selection advisors, VAR-channel commentators, and influential voices whose audiences include mid-market ERP buyers and channel partners.  Build and maintain active relationships with target analysts, positioning Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Advanced as platforms worth recommending — keeping analysts current on product direction, competitive positioning, and the partner program.  Drive a consistent cadence of introductions from analyst relationships: warm referrals from analysts to mid-market prospects actively evaluating or replacing ERP platforms.  Provide analysts with the product knowledge, competitive context, and reference materials they need to credibly recommend Intuit's mid-market platform to their audiences and clients.  Track analyst-sourced introductions through the attribution model, ensuring each qualified referral is tagged to the originating analyst and reflected in pipeline reporting. Digital marketing agency relationships

 Identify and recruit digital marketing agencies whose client base includes mid-market businesses with ERP needs — prioritizing agencies with active practices in verticals where IES has strong product-market fit.  Build the agency partner engagement model: define the value proposition for agency partners, develop the referral process and attribution mechanism, and create the co-marketing and lead-routing infrastructure that makes it easy for agencies to send leads to Intuit.  Enable agency partners on Intuit's mid-market product lineup and lead qualification criteria — ensuring that introductions from agencies meet the quality threshold for IES sales engagement.  Drive ongoing engagement with active agency partners: regular pipeline reviews, co-marketing activity, and program performance conversations.  Track agency-sourced introductions through the same attribution model as the analyst segment. Portfolio management & reporting

 Maintain an active and prioritized portfolio of analyst and agency partners, with clear visibility into relationship health, referral activity, and pipeline contribution per partner.  Identify underperforming relationships and develop targeted activation plans — additional enablement, co-marketing investment, or relationship reset as appropriate.  Report regularly on analyst and agency pipeline contribution to Felicia Wilson and the broader Commercial Partnerships leadership.  Surface market intelligence from analyst and agency conversations — buyer sentiment, competitive dynamics, and segment trends — to the IES product and go-to-market teams. Cross-functional collaboration

 Collaborate with the ISV Partner Manager and other Commercial BD colleagues to identify where analyst or agency relationships intersect with or amplify other partner motions.  Work with marketing to develop analyst-specific content programs, agency co-marketing campaigns, and thought leadership materials that strengthen Intuit's position in the mid-market ERP ecosystem.  Engage with the IES product team to keep analyst partners current on roadmap direction and ensure that Intuit's product story is compelling and accurate in analyst-generated content and recommendations.  Qualifications 

Required

10+ years of experience in channel partnerships, business development, or partner management within a SaaS or enterprise software company.  Familiarity with the mid-market ERP analyst and channel consultant community — you know who the influential voices are, how they operate, and what motivates them to refer business.  Demonstrated experience building commercial partner relationships and driving referral pipeline through those relationships.  Strong communication and relationship-building skills: able to engage credibly with independent analysts and digital agency principals, and to maintain productive long-term relationships with minimal formal program infrastructure.  Experience managing a partner portfolio with clear pipeline tracking and attribution discipline.  Proficiency with CRM tools (Salesforce preferred) and standard sales and partnership productivity platforms. Preferred

 Direct experience working with mid-market ERP channel analysts, software selection consultants, or VAR-channel commentators — you have existing relationships in this community.  Experience building agency partner programs, including referral process design, lead qualification frameworks, and co-marketing infrastructure.  Familiarity with Intuit Enterprise Suite, QuickBooks Advanced, or competing mid-market ERP platforms (Sage Intacct, Acumatica, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics). Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at [Intuit®: Careers | Benefits](#)). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender. The expected base pay range for this position is:

Albany $189,500 - $256,000
California Remote (Bay Area) $186,500- $252,500
Mountain View, CA $186,500- $252,500

entrylevelmarketingspecialistarizonacoin.description:
Company: Arizona Coin & Bullion / Adumu Inc. AI Systems & Software


Location: North Scottsdale, Arizona (On-site / Multi-location floating role)


Position Type: Full-Time, Entry-Level


About Us


Arizona Coin and Bullion is Scottsdale’s trusted premier destination for rare coins, precious metals, bullion, and numismatic expertise. Operating alongside our sister company, Lone Mountain Coin, we provide high-end collectibles and investment-grade precious metals in a client-first environment.


Beyond our coin shops, our parent group operates Adumu Inc. AI Systems & Software (adumu.com), an innovative technology firm building advanced tools like web data acquisition systems and local developer tooling. Because our operations span both physical retail luxury assets and cutting-edge software solutions serving both B2B enterprises and consumer markets, this is a unique, highly diverse entry-level career opportunity for a motivated marketing enthusiast looking to learn the ropes and grow across multiple industries.


Role Overview


We are seeking a dependable, creative, and detail-oriented Entry-Level Marketing Specialist to support brand awareness, social media, and digital campaigns across all of our enterprise businesses. This is a dynamic, "floating" marketing role—you will split your time and energy supporting our coin and bullion shops as well as our software company.


Whether you are helping craft social media content for rare coin collectors, shooting smartphone photos of new inventory arrivals, or assisting with digital marketing, community engagement, and user-facing content updates for our B2B and consumer software products, you will be a hands-on contributor across our entire portfolio.


No prior multi-industry or specialized marketing experience? No problem! We will teach you the ropes through comprehensive on-the-job training, but we are looking for a motivated self-starter who takes initiative, loves to learn, and wants a long-term home with real upward mobility.


Key Responsibilities


Content Creation & Social Media


Professionally photograph merchandise, retail items, and tech products using a smartphone or tablet.


Assist in creating engaging social media content, graphics, and short-form videos for platforms like Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and TikTok.


Help monitor active online listings, social channels, and community engagement for both our retail and software brands.


Digital Marketing Support


Assist with basic digital marketing tasks, email campaigns, and website/content updates tailored to a diverse audience—ranging from retail luxury precious metals buyers to B2B software clients and everyday tech consumers.


Help track and organize marketing assets, digital files, and campaign schedules.


Brand Collateral & Cross-Functional Support


Ensure consistent brand presentation across digital assets, in-store displays, and promotional materials.


Perform other duties and assist with cross-functional marketing and administrative tasks as assigned across our growing business operations.


What We're Looking For


Drive to Learn: No prior professional marketing experience required—just a hunger to learn, a creative eye, and the drive to work independently.


Tech-Savvy: Comfortable using computers, mobile devices, smartphones/tablets, and common social media, web, or content platforms.


Work Ethic & Integrity: Dependable with a strong work ethic and high integrity (trustworthy with company accounts, assets, and brand voice).


Organized & Self-Motivated: Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage tasks across multiple distinct businesses.


Physical Requirements: Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs. as required (for event materials or inventory) and stand/sit for long periods.


Requirements: Consistent and reliable attendance, plus the ability to successfully pass a background check as a condition of employment.


What We Offer


Pay: $18.00 – $25.00 per hour (based on experience)


Career Growth: Real opportunities for upward mobility and expanded responsibilities as our group of companies continues to scale.


Training: Comprehensive on-the-job training for someone ready to hit the ground running.


Environment: Stable, supportive, close-knit team located in North Scottsdale.


Schedule & Location


Schedule: Full-time, Monday through Friday plus Saturday (with a scheduled weekday off each week).


Environment: Based in North Scottsdale, with floating responsibilities coordinating across our retail coin shop locations and tech office environments.


Our Group of Companies Include


Arizona Coin & Bullion – (arizonacoinandbullion.com)


Lone Mountain Coin – lonemountaincoin.com


Adumu Inc. AI Systems & Software – adumu.com


Ready to start your career bridging physical wealth assets and futuristic B2B/consumer tech? Apply today!

principalspecialistcorporatecommunicatio.title: Principal Specialist, Corporate Communications
principalspecialistcorporatecommunicatio.description:
About GlobalFoundries:

GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com.

Summary of Role:

The Principal Specialist, Corporate Communications will be responsible for developing and executing strategic communications programs, messaging, and content initiatives that support the company’s corporate reputation and key policy, sustainability, and ESH priorities. This communications role will play a crucial part in amplifying GF’s leadership on issues important to the semiconductor industry, supporting issues and crisis communications, and translating complex technical and public policy topics into clear, compelling narratives for a range of stakeholders. The role will support executive communications, stakeholder engagement, and content development while partnering closely with Government Affairs, ESH, Sustainability, Legal, and site leadership teams to ensure consistent and effective communication across all channels.  
Essential Responsibilities:

  * Develop and execute communications strategies, messaging, and content that advance GF’s corporate reputation and policy, ESH, and sustainability priorities.
  * Draft and edit executive briefing materials, talking points, fact sheets, remarks, presentations, Q&A, and other communications for government engagements, site visits, hearings, industry events, community engagements, and other external forums.
  * Develop clear, accurate messaging on public policy and semiconductor industry issues, including CHIPS Act incentives, trade and export policy, workforce development, permitting, manufacturing competitiveness, and other matters affecting GF and the semiconductor ecosystem, based on positions established by Government Affairs.
  * Develop communications supporting GF’s engagement with government officials, industry associations, and other external stakeholders, including organizations such as the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) and SEMI.
  * Create and edit content for external channels, including corporate web content, thought leadership, op-eds, newsletters, social media, stakeholder communications, and other corporate materials.
  * Develop sustainability and ESH communications for GF’s annual sustainability reporting, corporate website, stakeholder communications, and other channels covering topics including energy, ultrapure water, greenhouse gas and process emissions, wastewater, waste, chemical management, and PFAS.
  * Partner with ESH and Sustainability subject matter experts to translate technical data, operational information, and environmental performance into clear, accurate, and accessible narratives for non-technical audiences.
  * Develop narrative content supporting ESG ratings, disclosures, questionnaires, and customer or investor inquiries, including CDP, with underlying data, policy positions, and final approvals owned by the appropriate functional teams.
  * Develop community and stakeholder communications related to fab operations, manufacturing expansions, construction, and environmental performance, including topics involving water, power, infrastructure, and potential impacts on neighboring communities.
  * Help lead communications planning for emerging issues and reputation risks, including the development of response statements, holding statements, Q&A, stakeholder messaging, and other issues-management materials.
  * Monitor policy developments, stakeholder issues, and relevant media coverage to identify emerging communications risks and opportunities and recommend appropriate communications approaches.
  * Maintain and evolve approved messaging, FAQs, briefing materials, and communications plans for priority policy, ESH, sustainability, and corporate reputation topics.
  * Develop internal communications that help employees understand GF’s policy, ESH, sustainability, and corporate reputation priorities and their connection to the company’s broader strategy.
  * Coordinate complex review and approval processes across Corporate Communications, Government Affairs, ESH, Sustainability, Legal, and site leadership to ensure communications are accurate, timely, and aligned.
  * Track relevant media coverage, stakeholder response, and content engagement to evaluate communications effectiveness and identify opportunities to strengthen future programs.



Other responsibilties:

  * Build strong relationships with communications partners and subject matter experts across Government Affairs, ESH, Sustainability, Legal, site leadership, and other functions.
  * Provide communications counsel and editorial guidance to internal stakeholders on complex, sensitive, or rapidly evolving issues.
  * Support issues and crisis communications as needed, including rapid development and coordination of executive and stakeholder communications.
  * Manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously, exercising sound judgment in a fast-paced, global environment.
  * Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.



Required qualifications:

  * Education: Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, public policy, English, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  * Experience: 4–5 years of experience in corporate communications, public affairs, public relations, or a related communications discipline.
  * Exceptional writing and editing skills, with demonstrated ability to translate complex technical, regulatory, policy, or environmental subjects into clear and compelling communications.
  * Demonstrated ability to quickly learn, synthesize, and communicate complex topics to technical and non-technical audiences.
  * Experience developing corporate messaging, executive communications, briefing materials, Q&A, stakeholder communications, or other strategic communications content.
  * Strong organizational and project management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, and deadlines.



Preferred qualifications:

  * Experience in the semiconductor industry, advanced manufacturing, electronics, energy, technology, or another highly regulated industry.
  * Experience partnering with Government Affairs, public policy, ESH, Sustainability, Legal, or similar functions in a corporate communications capacity.
  * Experience with issues management, crisis communications, media relations, community relations, or corporate reputation programs.
  * Experience communicating complex topics involving public policy, environmental performance, manufacturing operations, or sustainability.
  * Experience supporting senior executives and working across global, cross-functional organizations.
  * Project management skills, including the ability to innovate and execute solutions that matter and navigate ambiguity.
  * Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  * Strong planning and organizational skills.



Expected Salary Range

$72,000.00 - $126,000.00

The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location.

If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please contact us by email at usaccommodations@gf.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Requests for accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

Clients Blackbox is a performance marketing agency specializing in Meta advertising for Registered Investment Advisors.

We help financial advisors grow their practices by generating qualified appointments with high-net-worth prospects. Our proven video sales letter methodology has generated more than $45 billion in AUM pipeline for financial advisors across the country.

We operate with a performance-first mindset. Our clients hire us to deliver qualified appointments at a specific cost per appointment, with target show rates and close rates that make the economics work for their practice. Clients Blackbox is in a major growth period, and we're looking for a Paid Media Strategist / Account Strategist who can own client accounts from strategy through execution.

The Opportunity

This is a hands-on strategist role with responsibility for both client relationships and campaign performance. You'll own a portfolio of accounts, lead bi-weekly client calls, manage Meta campaigns, monitor results, contribute to ad messaging, and serve as the primary point of contact for your clients.

You'll report to the Associate Director of Operations and be directly accountable for client results, relationships, and retention.

What You'll Own

Client Strategy & Relationships



Own a portfolio of client accounts and serve as the primary point of contactLead bi-weekly client calls covering performance, strategy, priorities, and next stepsPrepare and send bi-weekly performance reports at least 24 hours before scheduled callsTranslate campaign data into clear, actionable recommendations for non-technical clientsBuild strong client relationships that support retention, renewals, and referralsSolve account issues proactively to support stability and growth

Meta Campaign Management

Build, launch, and optimize Meta campaigns focused on lead generation and appointment bookingManage budgets, audience targeting, bid strategies, creative testing, and campaign variablesMonitor performance daily and make adjustments based on cost-per-appointment and other key metricsDiagnose underperforming campaigns and develop strategies to improve resultsTest audiences, messaging, and creative to identify opportunities for stronger performanceContribute to ad copy and campaign messaging

Tracking & Technical Execution

Set up and troubleshoot tracking, Meta pixels, and conversion eventsConfigure Calendly integrations, Zapier automations, and lead-routing workflowsResolve technical issues between advertising platforms and client systemsProactively monitor tracking and lead flow to prevent issues from affecting client results

Copy & Creative Strategy

Write direct-response ad copy and video sales letter scripts for financial services audiencesDevelop hooks, angles, offers, and messaging variations for testingUse performance data to generate new creative and messaging hypothesesCollaborate with video editors and provide clear creative directionUse AI tools to accelerate research and copy development while maintaining quality and strategic judgment

Requirements

4+ years of hands-on paid media experience, with a strong focus on Meta advertisingExperience simultaneously managing multiple client accounts and leading client-facing conversationsProven ability to manage campaigns toward defined performance targets while supporting client retentionExperience with conversion tracking, pixels, and basic marketing automationStrong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills

Preferred Experience

Financial services marketingLead-generation and appointment-setting campaignsVideo sales letter marketingHigh-ticket or considered-purchase funnelsDirect-response advertising

How You Work

You take ownership. When something isn't working, you investigate the issue, determine what needs to change, and act. You're comfortable being accountable for results and explaining performance clearly to clients who may not speak marketing.

You're organized, detail-oriented, and able to move quickly across multiple accounts without losing sight of the outcome. You want to be responsible for making the account work - not one of several people sharing responsibility for it.

Note: AI and automated tools may be used in the application process. Every applicant is reviewed by a member of our hiring team, who makes the decision before anyone is disqualified. For questions or accommodations, contact natasha@clientsblackbox.com

Benefits

Paid Time Off, including vacation, sick time, and public holidaysTraining & DevelopmentWork From HomeFlexible SchedulePerformance Bonus

The Regional Field Lead is the commercial and strategic owner of a defined US fiber region, taking a hybrid, full 360 GTM and funnel approach to driving subscriber growth — responsible for translating national GTM priorities into a regional activation strategy, setting the sequencing and prioritization of market activity, and providing dotted-line leadership to a distributed team of Sr. Regional Marketing Managers to deliver against regional order volume and penetration targets. Mature market acquisition is the lead focus.

This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution. The Regional Field Lead does not run tactics directly — they build the strategic framework that Sr. Regional Marketing Managers execute from, ensure each market has the right plan for its archetype and competitive environment, and make the prioritization and resource allocation decisions that determine where the region wins and losses. They also own the regional view of channel partnership, performance management, and pricing and offers.

This is a remote role based in or near your assigned geographic region. You are a field leader — your team is distributed across a geography and you are expected to be present in it. Expect up to 40% travel within your region for market visits, Sr Regional Marketing Manager coaching, community and partner meetings, and launch activations. National travel for team planning and GTM Forum participation is also required.



JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

 

Regional GTM Strategy & Market Prioritization

Set the strategy.  Receive national commercial targets and translate them into a regional activation strategy — defining which markets get priority resources, which launch first, and what the sequencing logic is across the portfolioClassify and direct.  Classify each market in your region by archetype (Fiber Overlap, Greenfield, T-Mobile Dense, FWA Migration) and assign the corresponding strategy — messaging posture, offer stance and channel priority.Apply the 4Ps.  Build regional plans across Product, Price, Place, and Promotion, aligning offers, channel mix, and marketing to each market archetypeOwn the roadmap.  Build and maintain a 90-day regional activation roadmap that is updated monthly and reflects current market conditions, construction progress, and performance dataAllocate to impact.  Make resource allocation decisions across the portfolio — where to concentrate Sr. Regional Marketing Manager time, where to pull back, and where to escalate for additional support 

Market Transition

Partner with Emerging. Work alongside the Emerging team, which owns market launches, to set each market up to win. Then own the handoff as markets transition into the region, including the market strategy brief, performance to date, and open risks.Monitor and approve. Keep visibility on newer markets, flag early risks to Emerging while they can still be corrected, and approve each Sr. Regional Marketing Manager’s activation plan before it becomes mature.Represent the region. Present regional performance and market transition readiness, and recommend when a market is ready to move from Emerging. 

Regional Performance Management

Own the funnel.  Own the regional funnel end to end: Planned HHP RFS Commercially Launched Orders Installs Active Subs Penetration rate. Know where volume is being lost at every stage and direct action accordinglyDiagnose and act.  Identify which markets are on track, at risk, or in recovery — and make explicit decisions about what changes, not just observations about what's happeningDrive optimization.  Review CAC by channel and audience across the region. Identify where spend is working and reallocate toward the highest-performing combinations — don't wait for a quarterly review to move budgetEscalate with a plan.  Escalate red-threshold markets (below 3% penetration at Day 30) to the GTM Forum within five business days — with a specific recovery plan, not just a status updateBenchmark relentlessly.  Track penetration velocity curves for each market and benchmark against regional and national comps — know which of your launch engines is performing and which needs intervention 

Team Leadership & Sr Regional Marketing Manager Development

Lead to outcomes.  Provide dotted-line leadership to a team of Sr. Regional Marketing Managers embedded across the region — set clear expectations, review their plans, hold them to outcomes, and develop their strategic thinking over time. The Sr. Manager is their reporting manager, and you provide performance inputCoach, don't just check in.  Conduct weekly 1:1s focused on market performance, activation plan quality, and blockers — not status updates. You should already know the status; the 1:1 is for coachingManage to the individual.  Differentiate between a Sr. Regional Marketing Manager who needs strategic guidance and one who needs execution accountability — and manage them differentlyBuild the culture.  Build a team culture where proximity to target is the shared language — Sr. Regional Marketing Managers should know their numbers, understand why they're where they are, and have a plan to close the gap 

Cross-Functional Coordination

Connect the channels.  Serve as the regional point of contact for all sales channels, the Hyperlocal Strategy & Ops team, Operations, and JV partner field operations and construction — ensure local activation calendars are synchronized with channel timing and construction progress across the regionBe the regional voice.  Surface regional competitive intelligence, market conditions, and audience insights to the Sr. Manager and national GTM team on a regular cadenceConnect the dots.  Identify patterns across markets in your region — what's working in one market that should be deployed in others, and what failure mode is appearing in multiple markets that needs a regional responseOwn channel partnership and offers.  Manage channel partner performance across the region and bring non-standard offer and pricing recommendations to the GTM Forum, drawing on what the Sr. Regional Marketing Managers see locally 




QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's Degree plus 3 years of related work experience, or advanced degree with 1 year of related work experience, or combination of education and experience deemed equivalent7–10 years in field marketing, GTM, or market growth, preferably in B2C technology or service-related markets — with demonstrated ownership of commercial outcomes across a portfolio of markets or initiativesExperience leading a team of individual contributors, directly or indirectly and including distributed teams, and developing them toward greater strategic independenceHands-on understanding of hyperlocal marketing (local events tied to orders, community partnerships, street and ambassador teams, door hangers, direct mail), having led teams that executed itExperience in service-related or subscription go-to-market, including multi-location or geo-based marketingProven ability to translate a national or regional commercial target into a prioritized, sequenced market activation strategyStrong analytical fluency — reads funnel data, CAC reports, and penetration metrics and makes resource decisions based on what they sayExperience managing budgets and making spend allocation decisions under performance pressureTrack record of operating effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where the playbook is being built alongside execution, and resolving market-level escalations independentlyExperience executing across the 4Ps (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), including channel partnership, pricing and offers, and performance managementMarketing strategy and commercial acumen: audience segmentation, brand positioning, message hierarchy, channel mix, integrated planning, negotiation, partnership economics, media investment, and maximizing marketing ROIProven ability to brief senior executives with a point of view, not just a status, translating performance data into decisions, tradeoffs, and resource requests that hold up under challengeFiber or ISP go-to-market experience (ideal), or other home internet experience such as cable, DSL, or FWA preferredExperience coordinating field, CRM, D2D, and paid media channels in a unified GTM model preferredFamiliarity with competitive market dynamics and strategy adjustments based on competitive posture preferredExperience in market launch environments — building from zero and hitting velocity targets preferredAt least 18 years of ageLegally authorized to work in the United States

experience shaping a measurement roadmap.Comfort bridging brand and performance media; close partnership with creative, finance, product, and data science teams.How We Measure SuccessEfficiency and impact: CAC/CPA, CPQL, incremental contribution, brand lift, quality reach/frequency.Operational excellence: pacing accuracy, testing velocity and iteration speed, creative refresh cadence, percent of workflows automated, QA/brand safety adherence.Strategic influence: clarity of media strategy, improvements to the partner/tooling ecosystem, and durable cross-functional alignment.Location

94eradioandcommunicationssecurityrepaire.description:
Job Description

It’s extremely important that Army National Guard communications don’t fall into the wrong hands. As the Radio and Communications Security Repairer, you will maintain the equipment and systems that ensure Army National Guard units can communicate over secure channels.

Your duties will include installing and repairing circuits and wiring, calibrating and aligning equipment components, and stringing overhead cables between utility poles. Other duties include repairing systems, performing equipment tests, and performing preventive maintenance checks and services on equipment.

Advanced Radio and Communications Security Repairers take on more challenging projects, including training and supervising other Soldiers, testing equipment, performing complex repairs, and ensuring that the National Security Agency-approved components are used in communication security/controlled cryptographic item repairs.

Job Duties

 Use test, measurement, and diagnostic equipment; test program sets and interactive electronic technical manuals to troubleshoot and repair equipment

Some Of The Skills You’ll Learn

 Communication security policy and procedure

Helpful Skills

 Strong attention to detail

Through your training, you will develop the skills and experience to enjoy a civilian career in radio repair, radio mechanics, teletype repair, or station installation.

Earn While You Learn

Instead of paying to learn these skills, get paid to train. In the Army National Guard, you will learn these valuable job skills while earning a regular paycheck and qualifying for tuition assistance.

After 10 weeks of Basic Training, where you will learn fundamental Soldiering skills, you will attend Advanced Individual Training (AIT) for 16 weeks of classroom instruction, including practice with equipment. You will learn mechanical, electronic, and electrical principles, preventive maintenance procedures, and communication security policies and procedures.

Benefits/Requirements

Benefits

Paid trainingA monthly paycheckMontgomery GI BillFederal and State tuition assistanceRetirement benefits for part-time serviceLow-cost life insurance (up to $400,000 in coverage)401(k)-type savings planStudent Loan Repayment Program (up to $50,000, for existing loans)Health care benefits availableVA home loansBonuses, if applicableMost non-prior service candidates will earn between $200 and $250 per drill weekend, subject to change

Requirements

Military enlistment in the Army National GuardMust be at least a junior in high school, or have a high school diploma or a GED certificateMust be between the ages of 17 and 35Must be able to pass a physical exam and meet legal and moral standardsMust meet citizenship requirements (see NATIONALGUARD.com for details)
